judged_text: In Google `createEvent` (`CalendarService.ts` ~146-152) combined with EventManager's createAllCalendarEvents else-branch, legacy destination calendars with nullable `credentialId` never match `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, silently falling back to `calendarId: "primary"` — events are created on the wrong calendar while the stored reference gets `externalCalendarId: null`, routing later updates/deletes into the broken fallbacks; creation reports success while the real destination is wrong, and `organizer.email` is set to the legacy destination calendar's externalId which no longer matches the actual target calendar.

record.issue_text: In Google `createEvent` (`CalendarService.ts` ~146-152) combined with EventManager's createAllCalendarEvents else-branch, legacy destination calendars with nullable `credentialId` never match `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, silently falling back to `calendarId: "primary"` — events are created on the wrong calendar while the stored reference gets `externalCalendarId: null`, routing later updates/deletes into the broken fallbacks; creation reports success while the real destination is wrong, and `organizer.email` is set to the legacy destination calendar's externalId which no longer matches the actual target calendar.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows GoogleCalendarService.createEvent now selects the target calendar only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and otherwise uses `"primary"` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, when a destination calendar entry has no `credentialId` it takes the else-branch and calls `createEvent(c, event)` for each matching integration credential without passing any externalId, so the destination calendars in `event.destinationCalendar` (which may have `credentialId: null` in legacy data) will never match the `find(...)` and will silently fall back to primary. Additionally, `organizer.email` is still derived from the first destination calendar’s `externalId` (`mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`) even when the actual insert goes to `primary`, creating a mismatch. CalendarManager.createEvent returns `externalId` only if provided, but the else-branch omits it, so later references can lack the correct externalCalendarId.
